questions.prompt: What charge does a neutron carry?
options: No charge at all — it is neutral
The same charge as a proton
questions.explanation: A neutron is electrically neutral — it carries no charge, which is exactly why it is called a neutron.
questions.misconception: The positive charge belongs to protons and the negative to electrons — the neutron is the one particle with no charge at all.

questions.prompt: Carbon-12 has 6 neutrons and carbon-14 has 8. What are these two atoms called?
options: Isotopes — same element, different neutron count
questions.explanation: Atoms of the same element with different neutron counts are isotopes — both are carbon, just different weights.
questions.misconception: Since both have the same protons, they are the SAME element — only the neutrons differ, which makes them isotopes, not different elements.

questions.prompt: Where do neutrons live in an atom?
options: In the nucleus, packed with the protons
Between the shells and the nucleus
questions.explanation: Neutrons are packed into the nucleus alongside the protons — the dense core at the atom's center.
questions.misconception: All atoms have neutrons in their nuclei (except most hydrogen), and neutrons never orbit — they stay in the core with the protons.

questions.prompt: What does a neutron add to an atom?
options: Mass — it makes the atom heavier
Charge — it makes the atom positive
Color — it changes how the atom looks
questions.explanation: Neutrons add mass to the atom without adding any charge — heavier isotopes are heavier because of extra neutrons.
questions.misconception: Neutrons never change charge or electron count — their whole contribution is mass (plus nuclear stability).
